Isometric Log-Ratio Balance

Source: R/log_ratio.r
balance.Rd

One value per sample: the balance between two groups of features, the scaled log ratio of their geometric means. This is an isometric log-ratio balance (Egozcue & Pawlowsky-Glahn 2005), not a balanced design.

Usage

balance(counts, numerator, denominator, margin = 1L, pseudocount = NULL)

Arguments

counts

A numeric matrix of non-negative abundances (samples \(\times\) features), or any of the objects listed under Input Types. Counts, proportions, and the output of a zero replacement are all accepted: each sample's scale cancels out of the ratio.

numerator, denominator

The features on the top and the bottom of the ratio, each given as feature names, (1-based) feature indices, or a logical vector with one value per feature. Both are required, each must select at least one feature, and they must not share any. The two may use different forms (names for one, indices for the other).

margin

The margin containing samples. 1 if samples are rows, 2 if samples are columns. Ignored when counts is a special object class (e.g. phyloseq). Default: 1

pseudocount

Added to every value of counts before taking logs. NULL (the default) adds nothing when counts has no zeros, and otherwise uses half the smallest non-zero value of the whole table, with a warning, as ilr() does. 0 adds nothing, and gives NA for samples with a zero in a selected feature. See Pseudocount.

Value

A numeric vector with one value per sample, in the order of counts and named after the samples (unnamed if they have no names), whatever the margin. Larger values mean relatively more of the numerator. Attributes:

  • method: 'balance'.

  • numerator, denominator: the selected features' names (their indices when the features have no names), in the order of counts.

  • pseudocount: the pseudocount used (0 for none).

Its class, ecodive_log_ratio, gives it a short print() (a header naming the features, then the values) and a plot() by group or against a numeric variable (plot.ecodive_log_ratio()). Everything else treats it as a plain numeric vector (is.numeric() is TRUE); subsetting (x[1:5]), sort(), and arithmetic or maths (-x, x - mean(x), abs(x)) return a plain named vector without the attributes, which no longer describe the values.

Details

For a sample \(x\), numerator features \(N\) (\(r\) of them) and denominator features \(D\) (\(s\) of them), $$\mathrm{balance}(x) = \sqrt{\frac{rs}{r + s}}\,\log\frac{g(x_N + c)}{g(x_D + c)}$$ where \(g\) is the geometric mean and \(c\) the pseudocount (natural logs). This is the inner product of \(\mathrm{clr}(x)\) with the basis vector that has \(\sqrt{s / (r (r + s))}\) on the numerator features and \(-\sqrt{r / (s (r + s))}\) on the denominator ones: one row of scikit-bio's sbp_basis(). So balance() equals, to the last bit, the coordinate of ilr() whose row of a sequential binary partition has 1 on numerator and -1 on denominator (with the same pseudocount), without building the full basis. Features in neither group don't affect the value.

The factor \(\sqrt{rs/(r+s)}\) puts balances of different sizes on the same scale: each is a coordinate of an orthonormal basis, so their variances can be compared directly. Swapping numerator and denominator flips the sign. Like every log ratio, a balance is unchanged when a sample is multiplied by a constant (with no pseudocount). See log_ratio() for when to prefer the ratio of sums.

Balances are what selbal (Rivera-Pinto et al. 2018) selects, gneiss and PhILR build from trees, and coda4microbiome generalizes to log-contrasts.

Same names in other packages: compositions::balance() computes the same balances, with the same sign, from a formula (~ (A*B)/C); whichever package was attached last masks the other's. Write ecodive::balance() to be sure.

Pseudocount

A zero in any numerator or denominator feature makes its geometric mean 0, so zeros need replacing first. With pseudocount = NULL (the default), no pseudocount is used when counts has no zeros; otherwise half the smallest non-zero value of the whole table is added to every value, with a warning, exactly as ilr() does, so a balance agrees with the matching ilr() coordinate. To avoid a pseudocount, replace the zeros first with replace_zeros(): its result has none. With pseudocount = 0, samples with a zero in a selected feature get NA, with one warning naming them.

The choice of pseudocount is not neutral: it can distort the results, especially for sparse tables. See aitchison() for references.

Input Types

The counts parameter is designed to accept a simple numeric matrix, but seamlessly supports objects from the following biological data packages:

  • phyloseq

  • rbiom

  • SummarizedExperiment

  • TreeSummarizedExperiment

For large datasets, standard matrix operations may be slow. See vignette('performance') for details on using optimized formats (e.g. sparse matrices) and parallel processing.

References

Egozcue, J. J., & Pawlowsky-Glahn, V. (2005). Groups of parts and their balances in compositional data analysis. Mathematical Geology, 37, 795–828.

Rivera-Pinto, J., Egozcue, J. J., Pawlowsky-Glahn, V., et al. (2018). Balances: a new perspective for microbiome analysis. mSystems, 3, e00053-18.

See also

log_ratio() for the ratio of sums; ilr() for all the balances of a sequential binary partition at once; replace_zeros(); vlr(), rho_p() and phi_s() for finding features that move together.

Examples

    # Replace zeros first, then take the balance
    x <- replace_zeros(ex_counts, 'mult')
    b <- balance(
      x,
      numerator   = c('Streptococcus', 'Haemophilus'),
      denominator = c('Propionibacterium', 'Staphylococcus', 'Corynebacterium') )
    b
#> Balance of 2 over 3 features; pseudocount 0
#> Numerator:   'Streptococcus', 'Haemophilus'
#> Denominator: 'Corynebacterium', 'Propionibacterium', 'Staphylococcus'
#>    Saliva      Gums      Nose     Stool 
#>  3.938659  4.922648 -4.207824 -1.046615 

    # The first coordinate of ilr() with a partition that starts with it
    sbp <- rbind(
      c(1,  0, -1,  1, -1, -1),
      c(1,  0,  0, -1,  0,  0),
      c(0,  0,  1,  0, -1, -1),
      c(0,  0,  0,  0,  1, -1),
      c(1, -1,  1,  1,  1,  1) )
    all.equal(unname(b), unname(ilr(x, basis = sbp)[, 1]))
#> [1] "Attributes: < Modes: list, NULL >"                   
#> [2] "Attributes: < Lengths: 5, 0 >"                       
#> [3] "Attributes: < names for target but not for current >"
#> [4] "Attributes: < current is not list-like >"            
#> [5] "target is ecodive_log_ratio, current is numeric"
